# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 9 (Bu-Vb Sk9)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk9
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 9
**Title (English, from literature):** Lifting the robes

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Ukkhittaka* is the ninth training rule in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text sets out an etiquette rule concerning lifting the robes while among houses or inhabited areas. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. None of the surveyed secondary literature passages relate to this Vinaya rule, as all matching citations refer to unrelated texts such as the *Sāṃkhyakārikā* or Tibetan lists of siddhas.

The rule has widespread parallels throughout Buddhist monastic literature. Within the Pali tradition, it is paralleled in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 9), the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and the corresponding female monastic codes of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. Cross-sectarian parallels are attested in Sanskrit and Chinese versions belonging to the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda Vinayas for both monks and nuns.
